assets.purpose: Basic arrow tower, idle, single direction. Candidate A of T-0033, a roofed watchtower (steep pyramidal roof), selected by the human on 2026-11-06 and shipped over the previous open-battlement sprite. The design changed from battlement to roof because the generator cannot render a readable battlement at this scale (L-038); the roof is what it does well.
assets.prompt: tall stone watchtower with a steep conical/pyramidal roof, arrow slits and an arched door, isometric 3/4, isolated object on a transparent background, filling the frame: the roof smaller than the wall footprint with a visible overhang and eaves line, no flat roof slab, no crenellations or merlons, nothing clipped by the canvas edge, comparable to art/style/anchor.png

assets.content_size_detail: 28x53 is the pad-free content box including the 1px ink outline: bbox (18,11)-(45,63) of a 64x64 canvas, base on the bottom row, nothing clipped at any edge (x 18..45, so 18 px clear on the left and 18 on the right). Ground removed, so this is the L-034 figure. Measured on one consistent definition - the outline-inclusive silhouette, as the previous entry for this asset also reported - it is 28x53. The T-0033 return quoted 26x53; 26 is the width with the ink outline excluded, and the matching outline-free height is 51, so 26x53 pairs two different definitions. Both widths clear the 24 px floor; recorded here as the outline-inclusive figure to keep one definition for the asset.
assets.fill_rule: amended 2026-11-06 (art/STYLE.md 'Canvas fill'): roofed towers need height >= 80% of the canvas and widest row >= 24 px, because a roof tapers and cannot occupy a full tile width the way a flat-topped battlement can.
assets.fill_check: PASSES the amended roofed-tower rule on both counts: height 53/64 = 82.8% against 80%, easily clear; widest row 28 px against 24 px, clear by 4 px.
assets.top_row_width_profile: First rows top to bottom: 2,4,4,6,8,9,10,12,14,16,20,24,26,28,28 - monotonically widening, i.e. the roof tapers inward toward the top as required by T-0033 DoD item 2. A flat cut would hold or widen; this does not.

assets.design_change_note: The design changed from open battlement to roofed tower because the generator cannot render a battlement at this scale: it draws the top as a flat quad with no far wall, so hand-authored merlons read as free-standing blocks floating above it (L-038, rejected twice by the human). The roof plays to what the generator does well. This is a deliberate supersession, not a rendering regression.
assets.note: Disclosed identity drift: the body detail on this sprite is flatter than the previous battlement sprite - fewer distinct stone tones on the shaft (stone #8b8291 replaces the previous masonry shading) and less surface variation below the eaves. The silhouette and the tower's identity are preserved, the interior is simpler. Recorded rather than hidden; art/director conformance review of the roofed design is still outstanding even though the human selected this candidate.

generation_ledger.note: The vendor counter and the manifest do not agree and this block does not pretend they do. get_balance returns one cumulative number with no per-job breakdown, and the early job records have expired, so the individual costs of the early jobs are not recoverable from the vendor API. The seven evidence files registered under T-0092 therefore carry generations_spent: "unknown" rather than a guessed figure. Reconciling the two numbers would require inventing per-asset counts, which is worse than carrying an honest gap; what is recorded here is the size of the gap and the two attributions that did survive.
